channel.description: Recent content in Economics on Future Economists

item.title: The AI Productivity Gap: Why Faster Software Isn't Boosting The Economy
item.description: Despite trillions invested in AI infrastructure, global productivity remains flat—a modern echo of the Solow Paradox. Discover why faster software hasn't boosted the economy and what structural reforms are needed.

item.title: Inference Economics: Selling Intelligence
item.description: As AI spending hits $2.52 trillion annually, companies are discovering that the real cost isn't training—it's inference. Discover how the shift from SaaS to inference economics is reshaping corporate budgets and transforming software pricing models.

item.title: Quantum Computing & The Future Economy
item.description: From drug discovery to cryptography, quantum technology is projected to generate $100 billion in economic value by the mid-2030s. But what is quantum computing, and what is it used for?

item.title: Why Clean Energy Makes Sense, Economically
item.description: In 2024, 528 gigawatts of renewable energy were added to the global energy system, preventing $57 billion in fossil fuel usage while boosting economic growth and job creation.

item.title: Tokenomics: Explained
item.description: Why so some cryptocurrencies hold long-term while others fade away? A close look at the tokenomics of the project can explain how supply, demand, and incentives shape these outcomes.

item.title: Discover Our Mission
item.description: Future Economists is a student-created journal dedicated to researching how and why emerging technologies will reshape the global economic landscape.
